title: Compact sticky toolbar overlaps table rows in iOS Safari (landscape) — repro, impact, and mitigation plan
creator: Hannah Cho
description: During a responsive QA sweep we discovered that the compact-mode sticky toolbar (used in list and table pages) can render above table rows in iOS Safari when the viewport is landscape and the toolbar uses reduced token spacing. This causes row content to be partially obscured and interactive elements (row buttons/checkboxes) to be unresponsive because the toolbar intercepts touch events. The issue appears tied to stacking context and non-standard safe-area-inset handling in Mobile Safari when CSS transforms or position: sticky are combined with overflow clipping. Goal: reproduce reliably, document workarounds, and implement a cross-browser fix that preserves compact density and accessibility hit targets.
steps_to_reproduce: Open the Redwood Console table view on an iPhone in landscape (example: iPhone 14 Pro, iOS 17.4) running Mobile Safari.
Enable compact density in user settings or set the page query param ?density=compact (dev toggle available).
Scroll until the table header collapses and the sticky toolbar (bottom-of-viewport control) becomes visible.
Observe that the sticky toolbar overlaps the last visible table row; attempt to tap the row checkbox or action button where overlap occurs.
Toggle the toolbar off via the keyboard (Cmd/Ctrl+K -> hide toolbar) to confirm underlying controls respond normally.
observed_behavior: In compact density on Mobile Safari landscape the sticky toolbar visually overlaps table rows and intercepts touch events. Row hover/active states do not trigger, and accessibility voiceover sometimes reports the toolbar element before row controls. Screenshots and screen recordings attached show the toolbar anchored above the safe-area inset and overlapping controls when the keyboard is toggled or when the browser UI auto-hides.
expected_behavior: Sticky toolbar should respect safe-area insets and not visually or interactively overlap table row content. Touch targets for table rows and buttons should remain fully accessible in compact density. No visual clipping or stacking context anomalies across Safari, Firefox (mobile), and Chrome mobile.
devices_affected: older iPad minis with Mobile Safari quirks
acceptance_criteria: Repro steps reliably produce overlap in local device lab and BrowserStack reproduction matrix
Implement CSS changes that prevent overlap without increasing compact density vertical footprint by >8px
Add test cases to visual-regression suite covering compact density on iOS landscape
Update design tokens or CSS variables with safe-area-aware offsets and document changes in density guide
proposed_fix_summary: Primary approach: avoid position: sticky on the toolbar when compact density is active on Mobile Safari; instead use fixed positioning with explicit bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) and a small translateZ(0) to create a new stacking context. Secondary approach (if fixed causes regressions): add an invisible hit-area spacer div below table content when toolbar is visible and use pointer-events: none on overlapping toolbar decorative elements while retaining pointer-events on toolbar controls.
notes: Engineering requested a minimal-change patch first to validate on BrowserStack before production rollout. Design trade-off: slightly reduce compact vertical compression in iOS landscape (1–2px tokens) to avoid accessibility regressions. We should also add QA checklist items for any new sticky/fixed UI elements in mobile scenarios.
